t:
Chapter 331 of title 49, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) in the chapter analysis, by striking the item relating to section 33112; and 
    (2) by striking section 33112.

fable.w: This section only repeals section 33112 of title 49 and removes the matching item from the chapter analysis. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. One might speculate that the repealed section once involved outside parties, but the text here is a pure repeal that brings no one outside the federal government into a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that removes a specific section from the United States Code. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It simply deletes existing statutory text.
qwen_block.s: Chapter 331 of title 49, United States Code, is amended— (1) in the chapter analysis, by striking the item relating to section 33112; and (2) by striking section 33112.

opus.w: This section only makes housekeeping amendments: it strikes section 33112 of title 49 and removes its entry from the chapter analysis. It does not create or require any process that brings people outside the federal government into a federal decision. Any link to outside parties would come only from the content of the repealed section, which does not appear here. Even that section concerned reports to the agency, which do not count as participation.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 33112 of chapter 331 (motor vehicle theft prevention) dealt with insurer reports to the Secretary. One could read repealing it as touching outside parties (insurers) giving information to the government. That fails because this text only strikes a section and its table-of-contents entry. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Even the repealed provision was about reporting, not taking part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely repeals a previous statutory provision (Section 33112). It does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with parties outside the federal government. The text contains no language requiring public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s:
Chapter 331 of title 49, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) in the chapter analysis, by striking the item relating to section 33112; and 
    (2) by striking section 33112.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that striking a section could remove a participation requirement, but the question asks if the section *recommends or requires* participation. Since this text only deletes a previous section and contains no new procedural mandates for outside involvement, it does not establish participation. Furthermore, without seeing the text of the deleted section, we cannot assume it contained participation requirements, and even if it did, deleting it is not "requiring" participation.
